<reason>Both sides were excellent, but A (CON) built the cleaner path. A anchored everything in the motion's actual wording — "prioritize... over" — and exploited B's Rebuttal 1 concession that "the destination of the cargo is a detail," correctly noting this abandons the motion's core demand. A won the examples war: B never produced a single country that industrialized by prioritizing poor regional markets over distant rich ones, while A's list (Korea, Chile, Norway, Malaysia, Indonesia, Australia) all sold to rich markets. A's early concession of beneficiation ("refine the lithium, sell globally") neutralized B's value-capture, volatility, and jobs limbs, narrowing the debate to the destination question where the empirical record favored A. B fought back skillfully — the Q1 trap, the three concrete policies, the African import-demand argument, and the strong "they never defended dependence, only drift" close all landed — but B's answers on forex transition costs and the missing regional-first success story remained partial. A's clipped Rebuttal 2 was a minor cost since the substance was delivered. Grounding was disciplined on both sides with no fake sourcing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 1 turning B's "destination is a detail" line into a structural concession — "if that's true, half the motion just died" — which forced B to defend the destination limb for the rest of the debate and framed A's closing. Runner-up: A's levy paradox ("a levy either bites... or there is no priority at all"), which B only partially dissolved in closing.</best_rebuttal>
